concept: Badge is printing on the case of an appliance: a small status lamp with its own shape per tone and a word beside it, printed flat on the plastic with no box, no fill, no shadow and never orange.

default_to_avoid.pattern: coloured pill badge with white text (Bootstrap badge, Material badge)
default_to_avoid.why_not: A filled pill tells status by colour alone, tints the text, and adds a second loud shape to the unit next to the orange control.

default_to_avoid.pattern: status dot badge that changes only its colour between tones
default_to_avoid.why_not: A dot that only changes colour fails for colour-blind readers and in forced colours, so each tone needs its own shape and word.

references.source: Braun T 1000 world receiver (Dieter Rams, 1963): band names and indicator marks printed flat beside the keys
Braun ET 66 calculator (Dietrich Lubs, 1987): small printed marks and words on the case, no frames
system/refs/ref-01.png: lowercase model name printed on the inset line (estimated from chat)

derivation.consequence: printing is flat on the material — no shadow, no emboss
derivation.form: A badge has no box, background, border or shadow; the glyph and word are printed straight onto whatever plastic they sit on.

derivation.consequence: ink on plastic at ≥4.5:1 in both themes; no tinted text
derivation.form: The word is always text.primary; only the small glyph carries the tone's status mark colour, never the word.

derivation.consequence: links, borders, icons, selections and charts never use it
derivation.form: Tone marks come from status.positive-mark, warning-mark, critical-mark and info-mark; no tone, not even warning, uses the orange.

derivation.consequence: tabular figures everywhere a number changes
derivation.form: The count form prints its number in tabular figures and medium weight before the word, as in 3 offline.

derivation.consequence: labels sit on the body's inset line, never floating mid-surface
derivation.form: A badge is an inline line of printing that sits on the text line beside what it describes, never a floating corner bubble.

variants.reason: A is printing and nothing else, flat on the plastic (P5), with tone told by glyph shape plus word; B's frame makes a status look like a key people try to press (P3), and C adds a second display window per status, which P2 forbids.

root.why: An inline line of printing, glyph then word, that sits on the text line next to what it describes.

glyph.why: The status lamp is a small printed shape, flat on the plastic, with no glow, shadow or emboss.

word.why: The word is ink on plastic at 4.5:1 or more, never tinted with the tone, so it always reads.

count.why: A number before the word uses tabular figures in medium weight, so a changing count keeps its width.

neutral.why: Neutral is a hollow ring in secondary ink, a shape that says no particular state at all.

positive.why: Positive is a filled round lamp in the positive status mark, a green that is never the accent orange.

warning.why: Warning is a triangle in the warning mark with an ink edge, so the amber holds 3:1 against the plastic.

critical.why: Critical is a filled square in the critical mark, a shape that differs from every other tone's glyph.

info.why: Info is a diamond in the info mark, which is dark ink, so information never borrows a warm colour.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours every glyph is drawn in the text colour, and the shapes alone still tell the tones apart.
